classification.difficultyReason: Read ordinates and both intersections with horizontal lines from a supplied sine graph.

content.prompt: Use the graph of $\sin\theta$ to evaluate/solve. Give values in parts a–d to 2 decimal places and angles in parts e–h between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$, to the nearest degree.

spec.description: Editable sine graph with 10-degree by 0.1 minor grid, stronger 90-degree by 0.5 major grid, axis ticks and arrows. The incorrect source vertical-axis title is corrected to sine.
spec.mathematics: y=sin(theta), degrees; displayed grid 0<=theta<=360 and -1<=y<=1; curve continues slightly beyond 360 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph is visible in all editions; no response guides or answers are included.

answer.worked: At $\theta=25^\circ$, read the height of the sine curve: $\sin25^\circ\approx0.42$.
At $\theta=115^\circ$, read the height of the sine curve: $\sin115^\circ\approx0.91$.
At $\theta=220^\circ$, read the height below the horizontal axis: $\sin220^\circ\approx-0.64$.
At $\theta=310^\circ$, read the height below the horizontal axis: $\sin310^\circ\approx-0.77$.
Draw the horizontal line at $\sin\theta=0.6$. Read the angles at its two intersections with the curve: $\theta\approx37^\circ$ or $143^\circ$.
Draw the horizontal line at $\sin\theta=0.2$. Read the angles at its two intersections with the curve: $\theta\approx12^\circ$ or $168^\circ$.
Draw the horizontal line at $\sin\theta=-0.4$. Read the angles at its two intersections below the horizontal axis: $\theta\approx204^\circ$ or $336^\circ$.
Draw the horizontal line at $\sin\theta=-0.7$. Read the angles at its two intersections below the horizontal axis: $\theta\approx224^\circ$ or $316^\circ$.
